samples.summary: Restore-on-unlist only covers headings; `title`/`subtitle` blocks still lose their type irreversibly
samples.evidence: `unlistedBlockType()` keys entirely off `block.headingLevel`, and `MemDocStore.setBlockType` (memory.ts:260) / `YorkieDocStore.setBlockType` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1394) only remember `headingLevel`. `BlockType` also includes `'title'` and `'subtitle'` (types.ts:39), which sit in the same style dropdown (`blockTypeToStyleId`, text-style-options.ts:125-126). Bulleting a Title and un-bulleting it therefore still destroys the type and lands on `'paragraph'` — exactly the reversibility bug the task describes (#783), just for a sibling block type. The chosen representation (piggyback on the existing `headingLevel` field) cannot express "the block was a title", so the design does not generalize; a `previousType`-style memory would have covered all three. The task file's Non-goals (docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:49-58) list styling, splitting and DOCX/PPTX export — not title/subtitle — so this looks like an unacknowledged gap rather than a deliberate exclusion.
searchedFor: grep `title`/`subtitle` handling in blockStyleId and text-style-options.ts

samples.summary: Design doc claims "Google Docs / Word parity" for bulleted headings while the visible behaviour diverges
samples.evidence: The new section asserts parity because "bulleting a heading applies the bullet *to* the heading", but in this implementation the retained level is fully inert: `blockStyleId` maps every `list-item` to `'normal'` (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:99-113), so a bulleted Heading 2 renders and labels as body text (`getBlockLabel` returns "Normal text" for `list-item`, text-style-options.ts:106-114). In Google Docs a bulleted heading keeps its heading appearance and its style-dropdown label. The doc should record this divergence (the task file lists list-item styling as a Non-goal) instead of stating unqualified parity, otherwise the next reader treats the current rendering as the intended parity behaviour.

samples.summary: Bulleted headings silently drop out of the PDF bookmark outline (and markdown/DOCX heading output) with no design-doc note beyond "exports gate on type"
samples.evidence: `addOutlineFromHeadings` filters `b.type === 'heading'`, so once a heading is bulleted it disappears from the PDF outline; the same holds for `serialize/markdown.ts` (case 'heading') and `docx-exporter.ts:184`. The new design-doc text states this as a fact ("every reader … gates on `type === 'heading'`") but only DOCX/PPTX `pStyle` is listed as an intentional Non-goal, so the navigation/outline regression for bulleted headings is undocumented as an accepted consequence.
searchedFor: grep for an outline/TOC panel in packages/frontend/src/app/docs

samples.summary: Named-styles design doc still implies `headingLevel` only exists on `heading` blocks
samples.evidence: The style-mapping table (`heading` + `headingLevel: N` → `heading-N`) is the canonical description of how `blockStyleId` reads `headingLevel`; the data-model invariant changed (a `list-item` may now carry a level) but only docs/design/docs/docs.md was updated. A one-line note in the named-styles doc that a retained level on a `list-item` maps to `normal` would keep the two subsystem docs consistent.

verdict.reason: The factual core is accurate — I confirmed `unlistedBlockType` (types.ts:337-344) keys only on `headingLevel`, `MemDocStore.setBlockType` (memory.ts:249-263) and `YorkieDocStore.setBlockType` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1391-1413) remember only `headingLevel`, `'title'`/`'subtitle'` are real BlockTypes (types.ts:39) reachable from the unfiltered docs style dropdown (text-style-options.ts:34-44), and no `toggleList` implementation guards against bulleting them, so a bulleted Title does land on `paragraph`. I found no counterexample restoring title/subtitle anywhere. It is nonetheless not blocking under the design-fit rubric: the originating spec is explicitly heading-scoped (todo.md:1-32, steps 36-47 all satisfied), so no acceptance criterion is unmet and no stated Non-Goal is exceeded — the reviewer's own argument is that no criterion mentions title/subtitle. The chosen representation is a consciously documented design decision folded into the canonical subsystem doc (docs/design/docs/docs.md:117-134), not a parallel/missing doc, and title/subtitle round-trip behavior is unchanged by the diff (pre-existing). Preferring a `previousType` memory over a documented, justified minimal representation is a generality/taste preference = minor, which never blocks; it belongs in a follow-up issue or the task's Non-goals list.
